causeName: multi-feature account fold: planCountyParcelNodes collapses every txgio_parcel feature_index sharing one prop_id into ONE parcel-node atom, so the atom count is bounded by distinct accounts while the scorer's denominator counts distinct source features
causeEvidence: The fold is by design at packages/engine-core/src/parcel-node/plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:422-454 (Step 3, byAccount map keyed on parcelKey; extras counted into foldedExtraFeatures, one atom emitted per account). The writer at packages/engine-core/scripts/write-parcel-node-county.mjs:288-295 selects EVERY row for the county with no filter beyond county_fips, so nothing is skipped at read time; the entire reduction happens in the planner fold. Reproducing the planner's arithmetic in SQL predicts each county's atom count EXACTLY: predicted_atoms = count(distinct usable prop_id) + count(keyless features). Concho predicted 7629 actual 7629; Edwards predicted 9369 actual 9369; Lee predicted 15236 actual 15236; Atascosa 34707/34707; Cameron 175676/175676; Marion 18821/18821; Upshur 28723/28723; Fayette 22642/22642; Kerr 34939/34939; Wharton 30162/30162. In every one of the nine near-miss counties folded_extra_features equals the shortfall to the row (Concho 405=405, Edwards 579=579, Lee 854=854, Atascosa 2084=2084, Cameron 9386=9386, Marion 1020=1020, Upshur 1570=1570, Fayette 1240=1240, Kerr 1974=1974, Wharton 1726=1726). Synthetic keyless-feature atom counts also match prediction exactly (Concho 28, Edwards 213, Lee 468, Atascosa 59, Cameron 267). Competing causes are excluded: zero NULL feature_index in any county; feature_index space is dense 0..N-1 (Concho min 0 max 8033 distinct 8034); zero NULL geometry (Concho 7930 Polygon + 104 MultiPolygon, none null). Actual folded rows, Concho prop_id 2615 / geo_id PR26-1, 49 distinct feature_index values (2424,2426,5137,5775,5779,5780,5782,6568..6612) each with its own disjoint bounding box, e.g. feature 2424 bbox (-99.72570,31.53674,-99.72350,31.53770) and feature 6568 bbox (-99.72378,31.54083,-99.72191,31.54165), all vintage stratmap25-landparcels_48095_concho_202503. These are 49 physically separate real polygons sharing one CAD account, folded to one atom.

heterogeneousCauses.cause: multi-feature account fold (the band cause; geometry present, accounts shared)

prop_id column is not an account identifier at all — Ector's txgio_parcel.prop_id holds numeric-formatted values (0.00000000, 1576.00000000, 2077.00000000) with only 3,791 distinct values against 75,464 distinct geo_id and 75,891 features; this is a source/ingest column mis-mapping, a far more severe defect than the band fold and NOT the same root cause
same fold mechanism but at extreme magnitude compounded by a very high keyless-feature rate (24,241 keyless of 275,131 features, 8.8 percent, vs under 1 percent typical in the band)

proposedFix: Do NOT change the writer to emit one atom per feature — that would break the account-identity ruling the planner documents at plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:24-35 (Tarrant A 36-1 is 133 leasehold accounts on one polygon; account identity and geometry identity are deliberately separate). The defect is in the SCORER, not the writer: it divides an ACCOUNT-cardinality numerator by a FEATURE-cardinality denominator, which is a category error that can never reach 100 percent in any county where any account spans more than one feature. The correct cheap fix is to change the geometry rail denominator from count(distinct feature_index) to the number of features ACCOUNTED FOR by written atoms — i.e. count(distinct feature_index) minus foldedExtraFeatures, equivalently count(distinct usable prop_id) + count(keyless features), which is exactly the planner's own wouldWriteTotal. The planner already computes and returns this as counts.foldedExtraFeatures (plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:132, 452-453) and the writer already emits it in its summary, so the number needs no new computation, only to be persisted and used. Under that denominator all nine near-miss counties score 100.0000 percent, because predicted_atoms equals actual atoms exactly in every one. A secondary correctness improvement, independent of the score: add featureIndex (and the additionalFeatureIndexes list) to the atom's geometryStoreRef, which today carries only propId and countyFips, so a consumer following the pointer for a 49-feature account can tell which ring it gets. Ector 48135 must be excluded from this fix and routed separately as an acquisition defect — re-ingest keying on geo_id, or set --key-kind=geo_id_crosswalk, would take it from 3,791 to roughly 75,464 atoms.
ectorMechanism: Ector 48135 is NOT the same defect as the near-miss band and the existing 'multi-feature account fold' label for it is misleading. In the band counties prop_id is a genuine CAD account id that legitimately spans several platted features. In Ector, txgio_parcel.prop_id is not an account identifier at all: its values are numeric-formatted quantities (top values by frequency: '0.00000000' on 2,974 features, '1576.00000000' on 1,618, '2077.00000000' on 1,102, '114.00000000' on 968, '1814.00000000' on 737, '2600.00000000' on 686), consistent with an acreage or appraised-value column having been mapped into the prop_id slot during ingest. The county holds 75,891 distinct feature_index and 75,464 distinct geo_id — so per-parcel identity IS present in the data, on geo_id — but only 3,791 distinct prop_id. The planner keys on prop_id by default (write-parcel-node-county.mjs:316, keyKind: args.keyKind ?? 'prop_id'), so 75,891 real features collapse onto 3,791 pseudo-accounts, yielding exactly 3,791 atoms (verified: distinct prop_id 3,791 = atoms 3,791) and 5.00 percent coverage. Note the all-zero token '0.00000000' does NOT trip the isUsableKeyToken placeholder guard at plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:142-149, because that guard tests /^0+$/ against the trimmed string and the decimal point defeats it — so 2,974 features that should have become typed parcel-key-unresolved absences instead fabricated a shared account. Ector's fix is an acquisition/key-policy fix (re-key on geo_id), not a scorer fix, and it is worth roughly 71,673 additional atoms.
writerSkipConditions: packages/engine-core/scripts/write-parcel-node-county.mjs:288-295 — 'SELECT feature_index, tile_key, prop_id, geo_id, geometry, source_vintage FROM txgio_parcel WHERE county_fips = ${args.county} AND (feature_index, tile_key) > (${lastFeature}, ${lastTile}) ORDER BY feature_index, tile_key LIMIT ${pageSize}' — NO filter beyond county_fips; every row is read, so no parcel is skipped at acquisition-read time

packages/engine-core/src/parcel-node/plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:426-436 — 'const byAccount = new Map<string, FeatureView[]>();' ... 'const bucket = byAccount.get(view.parcelKey); if (bucket) bucket.push(view); else byAccount.set(view.parcelKey, [view]);' — THE FOLD: features are bucketed by account key, and one atom is later emitted per bucket regardless of how many features it holds

packages/engine-core/src/parcel-node/plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:447-454 — 'for (const [parcelKey, bucket] of byAccount) { bucket.sort(...); const primary = bucket[0]!; const extras = bucket.slice(1).map((v) => v.featureIndex); if (extras.length > 0) { multiFeatureAccounts += 1; foldedExtraFeatures += extras.length; } }' — the extra features are COUNTED into foldedExtraFeatures and then not written as atoms; this quantity is exactly the coverage shortfall

packages/engine-core/src/parcel-node/plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:473-485 — 'if (shape.kind === "reducible") { planned.push({ outcome: "resolved", featureIndex: primary.featureIndex, parcelKey, keyKind: primary.keyKind, additionalFeatureIndexes: extras, ... }); continue; }' — ONE resolved atom for the whole account, carrying the extras only as a reported list, never as separate atoms

packages/engine-core/src/parcel-node/plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:142-149 — 'function isUsableKeyToken(value: string | null): value is string { if (value === null) return false; const trimmed = value.trim(); if (trimmed.length === 0) return false; if (/^0+$/.test(trimmed)) return false; return true; }' — keyless features are NOT skipped, they become typed parcel-key-unresolved absence atoms under a synthetic key (lines 519-535), so they still count toward the numerator; note this guard fails to catch Ector's '0.00000000'

packages/engine-core/src/parcel-node/plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:488-502 — 'if (shape.kind === "multi-part") { absentByKind["geometry-incomplete"] += 1; planned.push({ outcome: "absent", ... }); continue; }' — multi-part geometry produces an ABSENCE atom, not a skip, so it does not reduce the numerator either
